title: Differential Relationships of Child Anxiety and Depression to Child Report and Parent Report of Electronic Media Use

primary_models.name: Generalized linear mixed model of parent-reported CBCL anxiety and depression T-scores on child-reported texting, social networking, and video chatting (weekday and weekend), adjusted for demographics, BMI and physical activity with site and family random effects
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 4 (anxiety, p. 913) and Table 5 (depression, p. 913); results text p. 913; interpreted in Discussion pp. 914-915.
primary_models.design: Cross-sectional analysis of the ABCD baseline visit. Screen-time predictors and CBCL outcomes measured at the same visit; one observation per child. Separate models for anxiety and depression and for each media category, weekday and weekend reports run separately. No longitudinal component.
primary_models.sample: ABCD baseline data (Annual Release 1.0; NDA data DOI 10.15154/1412097), 21 U.S. sites. Of 4524 children available, N = 4139 analysed after excluding cases with missing values, incomplete questionnaires, or 'do not know' responses; N is not reported separately per model. Ages 8.9-11 years (mean 10, SD 0.61); 1977 girls and 2162 boys; 15.2% Black American and 8.2% other minority backgrounds. Family income: 25% <= $49,999, 30.3% $50,000-$99,999, 44.7% >= $100,000.
primary_models.iv: Child-reported minutes per day of each phone/SM activity from the ABCD Youth Screen Time Questionnaire (STQ): texting, social networking, and video chatting, asked separately for a typical weekday and weekend day. Response options range from '0 h' (0) to '4+ h' (4); the paper describes converting hours to minutes (x60) for total EMU, and Table 1 gives category ranges of 0-240 min. Each modality (weekday or weekend) is entered as the predictor; the paper does not state explicitly whether each category was run in its own model or all categories were entered jointly, but the parallel structure with the general-EMU analyses suggests one category per model. All variables were standardized before analysis. Table 1 (p. 911) descriptives (mean, SD): weekday texting 11.99, 0.51; social networks 5.55, 0.36; video chatting 9.04, 0.41; weekend texting 13.86, 0.60; social networks 6.97, 0.45; video chatting 11.21, 0.52. The printed SDs are implausibly small relative to means in minutes and may be in hours or category units.
primary_models.dv: Parent-reported Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) T-scores, analysed as continuous outcomes: anxiety subscale (9 items, 0-2 scale; sample M = 53.37, SD = 5.939, range 50-94, Table 1) and depression subscale (13 items, 0-2 scale; sample M = 53.43, SD = 5.57, range 50-89, Table 1). Both standardized before analysis.

primary_models.equation: z(CBCL_DV)[i] = b0 + b1*z(phoneSM_IV)[i] + b2*z(age) + b3*z(sex) + b4*z(BMI) + b5*z(family_income) + b6*z(race) + b7*z(physical_activity) + u_site + u_family + e[i]; b1 is the standardized coefficient reported in Tables 4-5.
primary_models.estimation: IBM SPSS Statistics v25, generalized linear mixed models with nesting within testing site and family (random effects). All variables standardized, so coefficients are interpreted as standardized betas (Discussion p. 915: 'standardized beta weights'). alpha = 0.05; no multiple-comparison correction. Parallel models additionally controlling for depression (anxiety DV) or anxiety (depression DV) are reported in Supplemental Tables 1-2, which are not in the PDF; Tables 4-5 only flag with footnote a which estimates stayed significant. Sex moderation was tested via EMU x sex interaction terms; only child-reported weekend EMU x sex predicting anxiety was significant, which led to the sex-stratified models in M2.

primary_models.name: Sex-stratified generalized linear mixed model of CBCL anxiety T-score on child-reported weekend texting, social networking, and video chatting, adjusted for demographics, BMI and physical activity with site and family random effects
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 3 (p. 912); results text p. 912 ('Sex Differences') and p. 913; interpreted in Discussion p. 914.
primary_models.design: Cross-sectional ABCD baseline, same as M1, but fitted separately in boys and girls. Run only for child-reported weekend EMU predicting anxiety, because that was the only significant EMU x sex interaction (for overall weekend EMU, t = -3.51, p < .001).
primary_models.sample: Same ABCD Release 1.0 baseline analytic sample as M1 (N = 4139), split by sex: boys (2162) and girls (1977). Per-stratum Ns for these models are not printed; the counts given are the sample sex breakdown from Participants (p. 909).
primary_models.iv: Child-reported weekend minutes per day of texting, social networking, and video chatting (ABCD Youth STQ), standardized. Weekend descriptives for the full sample (Table 1): texting M = 13.86, SD printed 0.60; social networks M = 6.97, SD 0.45; video chatting M = 11.21, SD 0.52. Sex-specific descriptives not reported.
primary_models.dv: Parent-reported CBCL anxiety subscale T-score (continuous), standardized. Full-sample M = 53.37, SD = 5.939.

d_transformation.conversion_formula: Standardized beta treated as approximate r: d = 2 * beta_std / sqrt(1 - beta_std^2), applied to the coefficient and to each CI bound (guidelines §4a).
d_transformation.contrast_type: per 1 SD of the child-reported phone/SM minutes per day (weekday or weekend), in SD units of the CBCL T-score
d_transformation.notes: All variables were standardized before modelling (Data Analysis, p. 910; Discussion p. 915 calls them 'standardized beta weights'), so no SD_IV/SD_DV is needed; sd_iv and sd_dv are left null. Table 1 (p. 911) SDs are recorded in iv_axis meta for reference but look implausible for minute-scale variables (e.g., weekday texting M = 11.99, SD = 0.51, range 0-240) and should not be used for rescaling. Because the outcome variables were also standardized, using the sample CBCL SDs (anxiety 5.939, depression 5.57) rather than the normative T-score SD of 10 is implicit in the coefficients. Effects are adjusted for covariates with partial-out of site/family random effects, so the beta-as-r approximation is approximate.

extraction_flags:
1. Anchoring model: the authors also read their findings off parallel models that control for depression or anxiety. Those coefficients are in Supplemental Tables 1-2, which are online only and not in the PDF. Only footnote 'a' flags in Tables 3-5 show which estimates stayed significant. I extracted the printed versions without that control (Tables 4/5 for the full sample, Table 3 sex-stratified) and listed the controlled versions under excluded models. If the supplement can be obtained, add those coefficients.

2. Separate or joint models: the paper does not say whether each media category was its own GLMM or all categories went into one model. I assumed one category per model.

3. Coefficients are treated as standardized betas because the paper says all variables were standardized. The SPSS link function / GLMM family is not stated; I assumed linear on continuous T-scores.

4. Table 1 SDs for the media categories look implausible (e.g., weekday texting mean 11.99 min, SD 0.51, range 0-240). They are recorded only as meta. sd_iv and sd_dv are left null because the betas are already standardized.

5. M2 (sex-stratified, weekend only) has no per-stratum N. The 2162 boys and 1977 girls are the full-sample sex counts.

6. ABCD release is inferred as 1.0 from reference 36 and the NDA DOI.
